Military Governor of the Yicheng Army

Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent
Military Commissioner of the Kuangguo Army

units.zh: 和凝，字成績，鄆州須昌人也。
units.en: He Ning, whose courtesy name was Chengji, came from Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: He Ning, courtesy name Chengji, was a native of Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 其九世祖逢堯為唐監察御史，其後世遂不復宦學。
units.en: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao had been a Tang surveillance censor, and for generations afterward the family ceased to pursue office and learning.
units.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao had served as a Tang surveillance censor; thereafter the family no longer pursued official study.

units.zh: 凝父矩，性嗜酒，不拘小節，然獨好禮文士，每傾貲以交之，以故凝得與之遊。
units.en: Ning's father Ju loved wine and cared little for petty propriety, yet he alone delighted in honoring men of letters and would spend his fortune to befriend them, which allowed young Ning to move in their circles.
units.literal: Ning's father Ju was by nature fond of wine and heedless of minor proprieties, yet he alone delighted in honoring literary gentlemen and would exhaust his wealth to befriend them; for this reason Ning was able to associate with them.

units.zh: 而凝幼聰敏，形神秀發。
units.en: As a boy, Ning was clever and quick-witted, with a bright and striking bearing.
units.literal: Ning in youth was clever and quick, with a bright and striking presence.

units.zh: 舉進士，梁義成軍節度使賀瑰辟為從事。
units.en: After passing the jinshi examination, he was recruited as an aide by He Gui, military governor of the Liang Yicheng Army.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; He Gui, military governor of the Liang Yicheng Army, recruited him as an aide.

units.zh: 瑰與唐莊宗戰於胡柳，瑰戰敗，脫身走，獨凝隨之，反顧見凝，麾之使去。
units.en: At Hulu, He Gui fought Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang and was defeated. He broke away and fled, but He Ning alone stayed with him. Gui looked back, saw Ning, and gestured for him to go.
units.literal: Gui fought Tang's Zhuangzong at Hulu; Gui was defeated, broke away and fled, and Ning alone followed him. Gui looked back, saw Ning, and waved for him to leave.

units.zh: 凝曰：「丈夫當為知己死，吾恨未得死所爾，豈可去也！」
units.en: Ning said: "A man should die for his patron. I only regret that I have not yet found the place to die—how could I leave!"
units.literal: Ning said: "A man ought to die for one who knows him; I regret only that I have not yet found the place to die—how could I leave!"

units.zh: 已而一騎追瑰幾及，凝叱之不止，即引弓射殺之，瑰由此得免。
units.en: Soon a lone rider was almost upon Gui. Ning shouted for him to halt, but he would not stop, so Ning drew his bow and shot him dead, and Gui was saved.
units.literal: Before long a single rider pursued Gui and nearly caught up. Ning shouted at him but he would not stop; Ning then drew his bow and shot him dead, and Gui thereby escaped.

units.zh: 瑰歸，戒其諸子曰：「和生，誌義之士也，後必富貴，爾其謹事之！」
units.en: When Gui returned home, he told his sons: "Young He is a man of principle and resolve and will surely rise to wealth and rank. You must respect and serve him well!"
units.literal: When Gui returned, he admonished his sons: "Young He is a man of principle and resolve; he is sure to become rich and noble hereafter—you must serve him carefully!"

units.zh: 因妻之以女。
units.en: He then gave him his daughter in marriage.
units.literal: He therefore gave him his daughter in marriage.

units.zh: 天成中，拜殿中侍御史，累遷主客員外郎，知制誥，翰林學士，知貢舉。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era he was made palace attendant censor, then successively bureau director in the Ministry of Rites for Receiving Guests, drafter of edicts, Hanlin academician, and supervisor of the examinations.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor, and was successively promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites for Receiving Guests, took charge of drafting edicts, became Hanlin Academician, and supervised the examinations.

units.zh: 是時，進士浮薄，喜為喧嘩以動主司。
units.en: At that time jinshi candidates were shallow and unruly, and liked to raise noisy demonstrations to pressure the chief examiners.
units.literal: At that time jinshi candidates were frivolous and shallow, and liked to raise clamorous outcries to sway the chief examiners.

units.zh: 主司每放榜，則圍之以棘，閉省門，絕人出入以為常。
units.en: Whenever results were posted, the examiners would surround the area with thorn hedges, close the ministry gates, and bar all traffic—a routine precaution.
units.literal: Each time the chief examiners announced the results, they would surround the area with thorn hedges, close the ministry gates, and cut off all coming and going as a regular practice.

units.zh: 凝徹棘開門，而士皆肅然無嘩，所取皆一時之秀，稱為得人。
units.en: Ning removed the thorn hedges and opened the gates. The candidates remained orderly and silent. Those he selected were the finest scholars of the day, and he was praised for choosing well.
units.literal: Ning cleared away the thorns and opened the gates, yet the candidates were all solemn and raised no clamor; those he selected were all the finest men of the age, and people praised him for choosing well.

units.zh: 晉初，拜端明殿學士，兼判度支，為翰林學士承旨。
units.en: Early in the Jin dynasty he was made academician of the Duanming Hall, concurrently supervisor of the Treasury Bureau, and chief Hanlin academician.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, concurrently supervising the Treasury Bureau, and became chief Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 高祖數召之，問以時事，凝所對皆稱旨。
units.en: Gaozu repeatedly summoned him to discuss current affairs, and Ning's answers always pleased him.
units.literal: Gaozu repeatedly summoned him and questioned him on current affairs; Ning's replies all pleased him.

units.zh: 天福五年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 高祖將幸鄴，而襄州安從進反迹已見。
units.en: Gaozu was preparing to visit Ye when signs that An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture would rebel had already appeared.
units.literal: Gaozu was about to visit Ye when signs of rebellion by An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture had already appeared.

units.zh: 凝曰：「陛下幸鄴，從進必因此時反，則將奈何？」
units.en: Ning said, "If Your Majesty visits Ye, Congjin will surely rebel at that moment—what then shall we do?"
units.literal: Ning said: "If Your Majesty visits Ye, Congjin will surely rebel at this time—what then shall we do?"

units.zh: 高祖曰：「卿將何以待之？」
units.en: Gaozu asked, "How would you handle it?"
units.literal: Gaozu said: "How will you deal with it?"

units.zh: 凝曰：「先人者，所以奪人也。
units.en: Ning said, "To strike first is to seize the initiative from others.
units.literal: Ning said: "To act first is to seize the initiative from others.

units.zh: 請為宣敕十餘通，授之鄭王，有急則命將擊之。」
units.en: Prepare more than ten blank edicts and give them to the Prince of Zheng; if there is an emergency, he can order generals to attack."
units.literal: Please prepare more than ten blank edicts and give them to the Prince of Zheng; in an emergency he can order generals to strike."

units.zh: 高祖以為然。
units.en: Gaozu agreed.
units.literal: Gaozu thought this correct.

units.zh: 是時，鄭王為開封尹，留不從幸，乃授以宣敕。
units.en: At that time the Prince of Zheng was metropolitan prefect of Kaifeng and stayed behind rather than accompany the tour; he was given the blank edicts.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Zheng was metropolitan prefect of Kaifeng and remained behind rather than accompany the tour; he was given the blank edicts.

units.zh: 高祖至鄴，從進果反，鄭王即以宣敕命騎將李建崇、焦繼勳等討之。
units.en: When Gaozu reached Ye, Congjin rebelled as expected. The Prince of Zheng immediately used the blank edicts to order cavalry generals Li Jianchong, Jiao Jixun, and others to suppress him.
units.literal: When Gaozu reached Ye, Congjin did rebel. The Prince of Zheng immediately used the blank edicts to order cavalry generals Li Jianchong, Jiao Jixun, and others to campaign against him.

units.zh: 從進謂高祖方幸鄴，不意晉兵之速也，行至花山，遇建崇等兵，以為神，遂敗走。
units.en: Congjin assumed Gaozu was still at Ye and did not expect Jin troops to move so quickly. At Huashan he met Jianchong and the others, took them for a miracle, and fled in defeat.
units.literal: Congjin thought Gaozu was still visiting Ye and did not expect Jin troops to arrive so swiftly. Marching to Huashan, he met Jianchong and the others, took them for divine intervention, and fled in defeat.

units.zh: 出帝即位，加右僕射，歲餘，罷平章事，遷左僕射。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Ning was promoted to right vice director. After more than a year he was removed as grand councilor and made left vice director.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Ning was promoted to Right Vice Director. After more than a year he was removed as grand councilor and transferred to Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 漢高祖時，拜太子太傅，封魯國公。
units.en: Under Han Gaozu he was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
units.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

units.zh: 顯德二年卒，年五十八，贈侍中。
units.en: In the second year of Xiande he died at fifty-eight and was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.
units.literal: In the second year of Xiande he died at age fifty-eight and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 凝好飾車服，為文章以多為富，有集百餘卷，嘗自鏤板以行於世，識者多非之。
units.en: Ning loved to dress his carriage and robes lavishly. In writing he equated abundance with quality. He compiled more than a hundred scrolls and had them block-printed for public circulation—an act widely criticized by the discerning.
units.literal: Ning loved to adorn his carriage and robes; in writing essays he took quantity for wealth. He had a collection of more than a hundred scrolls and once carved blocks himself to circulate them in the world; men of discernment mostly criticized this.

units.zh: 然性樂善，好稱道後進之士。
units.en: Yet by nature he delighted in doing good and liked to praise and promote younger scholars.
units.literal: Yet by nature he delighted in doing good and liked to praise and commend rising scholars.

units.zh: 唐故事，知貢舉者所放進士，以己及第時名次為重。
units.en: By Tang custom, the exam supervisor who passed candidates placed special significance on the rank at which he himself had passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: By Tang custom, when the supervisor of examinations released jinshi, he attached special weight to the ranking he himself had received when he passed the examination.

units.zh: 凝舉進士及第時第五，後知舉，選範質為第五。
units.en: When Ning himself had passed the jinshi he ranked fifth; later, as exam supervisor, he placed Fan Zhi fifth.
units.literal: When Ning passed the jinshi examination he ranked fifth; later when he supervised the examinations he selected Fan Zhi as fifth.

units.zh: 後質位至宰相，封魯國公，官至太子太傅，皆與凝同，當時以為榮焉。
units.en: Later Fan Zhi rose to chancellor, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and reached the post of grand preceptor of the heir apparent—all mirroring Ning's own career, which contemporaries took as an honor to them both.
units.literal: Later Zhi rose to the rank of chancellor, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and reached the office of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent—all the same as Ning's—and the age regarded it as an honor.

units.zh: 趙瑩，字玄輝，華州華陰人也。
units.en: Zhao Ying, whose courtesy name was Xuanhui, came from Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhao Ying, courtesy name Xuanhui, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 為人純厚，美風儀。
units.en: He was sincere and solid in character, with a dignified bearing.
units.literal: As a man he was pure and solid, with a fine bearing.

units.zh: 事梁將康延孝為從事。
units.en: He served the Later Liang general Kang Yanxiao as an aide.
units.literal: He served the Later Liang general Kang Yanxiao as an aide.

units.zh: 晉高祖為保義軍節度使，以瑩掌書記，自是徙鎮常以瑩從。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin was military governor of the Baoyi Army, he made Ying his secretary; thereafter, whenever he changed postings, Ying usually accompanied him.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin was military governor of the Baoyi Army, he had Ying serve as secretary; from then on, whenever he was transferred to another post he usually took Ying with him.

units.zh: 高祖將起兵太原，以問諸將吏，將吏或贊成之，瑩獨懼形於色，勸高祖毋反。
units.en: When Gaozu was about to raise troops at Taiyuan, he consulted his generals and officials. Some approved, but Ying alone showed his fear openly and urged Gaozu not to rebel.
units.literal: When Gaozu was about to raise troops at Taiyuan, he questioned the various generals and officials. Some generals and officials approved it; Ying alone showed fear in his expression and advised Gaozu not to rebel.

units.zh: 高祖雖不用其言，心甚愛之。
units.en: Gaozu did not heed his advice, but cherished him all the more for his honesty.
units.literal: Although Gaozu did not adopt his words, in his heart he greatly cherished him.

units.zh: 高祖即位，拜翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Ying was made chief Hanlin academician, vice minister of revenue, and associate grand councilor.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed chief Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and Associate Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 累拜中書令。
units.en: He was subsequently promoted to secretariat director.
units.literal: He was successively appointed Secretariat Director.

units.zh: 出為晉昌軍節度使、開封尹。
units.en: He was sent out to serve as military governor of the Jinchang Army and prefect of Kaifeng.
units.literal: He was sent out as military governor of the Jinchang Army and prefect of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 是時，出帝童昏，馮玉、李彥韜等用事，與桑維翰爭權，乃共譖去之，以瑩柔而易制，故復引以為相。
units.en: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and inexperienced. Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power and were locked in a struggle with Sang Weihan. They conspired to remove Sang, and because Ying was gentle and pliable, brought him back as chancellor.
units.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and dull; Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power and contended for authority with Sang Weihan. They therefore jointly slandered him until he was removed. Because Ying was gentle and easy to control, they again brought him in as chancellor.

units.zh: 契丹滅晉，瑩從出帝北徙虜中，瑩事兀欲為太子太保。
units.en: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Ying followed the Deposed Emperor north into captivity and served Wuyu as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Khitan destroyed Jin, Ying followed the Deposed Emperor north into captivity. Ying served Wuyu as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 周太祖時，與契丹通好，遣尚書左丞田敏使於契丹，遇瑩於幽州，瑩見敏悲不自勝。
units.en: During Taizu of Zhou's reign, when peace was made with the Khitan, Tian Min was sent as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou, and Ying wept uncontrollably at the sight of him.
units.literal: During Zhou Taizu's time, when peace was made with Khitan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Min was sent on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou; when Ying saw Min he was so grief-stricken he could not contain himself.

units.zh: 瑩子易則、易從。
units.en: Ying had two sons, Yize and Yicong.
units.literal: Ying's sons were Yize and Yicong.

units.zh: 當其徙而北也，與易從俱，而易則留事漢，官至刑部郎中。
units.en: When Ying was taken north, he went with Yicong, while Yize remained to serve the Han court and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
units.literal: When he was moved north, he went with Yicong, while Yize remained to serve Han and reached the office of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.

units.zh: 後瑩病將卒，告於契丹，願以屍還中國，契丹許之。
units.en: Later, when Ying fell gravely ill, he asked the Khitan to allow his body to be returned to China, and they agreed.
units.literal: Later when Ying fell ill and was near death, he informed Khitan that he wished his corpse returned to China; Khitan granted it.

units.zh: 及卒，遣易從護其喪南歸。
units.en: When he died, Yicong was sent to escort his coffin back south.
units.literal: When he died, Yicong was sent to escort his coffin south in return.

units.zh: 太祖憐之，贈瑩太傅，葬於華陰。
units.en: Taizu took pity on him, posthumously granted Ying the title of grand preceptor, and had him buried at Huayin.
units.literal: Taizu took pity on him, posthumously granted Ying the title of Grand Preceptor, and buried him at Huayin.

units.zh: 馮玉，字璟臣，定州人也。
units.en: Feng Yu, whose courtesy name was Jingchen, came from Ding Prefecture.
units.literal: Feng Yu, courtesy name Jingchen, was a native of Ding Prefecture.

units.zh: 少舉進士不中。
units.en: As a young man he took the jinshi examination but failed.
units.literal: In youth he took the jinshi examination but did not pass.

units.zh: 馮赟為河東節度使，辟為推官。
units.en: When Feng Yun was military governor of Hedong, he recruited Yu as an investigating officer.
units.literal: When Feng Yun was military governor of Hedong, he recruited Yu as investigating officer.

units.zh: 入拜監察御史，累遷禮部郎中，為鹽鐵判官。
units.en: He entered the capital as surveillance censor, was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and served as salt and iron commissioner.
units.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Surveillance Censor, was successively promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, and served as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

units.zh: 晉出帝納玉姊為後，玉以後戚知制誥，拜中書舍人。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor of Jin took Yu's elder sister as empress. As a maternal relative of the empress, Yu was put in charge of drafting edicts and appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor of Jin took Yu's elder sister as empress. Yu, as a maternal relative of the empress, took charge of drafting edicts and was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 玉不知書，而與殷鵬同為舍人，制誥常遣鵬代作。
units.en: Yu was illiterate, yet he and Yin Peng both served as drafting secretaries; edicts were routinely sent to Peng to write in his stead.
units.literal: Yu did not know the written word, yet he and Yin Peng were both drafting secretaries; edicts were usually sent for Peng to draft in his place.

units.zh: 頃之，玉出為潁州團練使，拜端明殿學士、戶部侍郎，遷樞密使、中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Before long Yu was sent out as military training commissioner of Ying Prefecture, then appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue, and finally promoted to privy commissioner, vice director of the Secretariat, and associate grand councilor.
units.literal: Before long Yu was sent out as military training commissioner of Ying Prefecture, was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of Revenue, and was transferred to Privy Commissioner, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Associate Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 是時，出帝童昏，馮皇后用事，軍國大務，一決於玉。
units.en: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and inexperienced. Empress Feng held sway, and all major affairs of state and army were decided by Yu alone.
units.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and dull; Empress Feng held power, and all great affairs of state and army were decided entirely by Yu.

units.zh: 玉嘗有疾在告，自刺史已上，宰相不敢除授，以俟玉決。
units.en: When Yu once took sick leave, the chancellors dared not appoint anyone from prefect upward until Yu had decided.
units.literal: Yu once had an illness and was on leave. From prefect and up, the chancellors dared not make appointments, waiting for Yu's decision.

units.zh: 玉除中書舍人盧價為工部侍郎，桑維翰以價資望淺為不可，由是與維翰有隙，維翰由此罷相。
units.en: Yu appointed drafting secretary Lu Jia as vice minister of works. Sang Weihan objected that Jia's seniority and reputation were too slight, and a rift opened between them. Weihan was removed from the chancellery as a result.
units.literal: Yu appointed Drafting Secretary Lu Jia as Vice Minister of Works. Sang Weihan held that Jia's seniority and reputation were too shallow and objected that it was impossible; thereby Yu and Weihan had a breach, and Weihan was thereby removed as chancellor.

units.zh: 玉為相，四方賄，積貲巨萬。
units.en: As chancellor, Yu took bribes from all quarters and amassed a fortune.
units.literal: As chancellor Yu received bribes from all quarters and amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 契丹滅晉，張彥澤先以兵入京師，兵士爭先入玉家，其貲一夕而盡。
units.en: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Zhang Yanzhe was first to enter the capital with troops. Soldiers raced to plunder Yu's house, and his fortune was gone overnight.
units.literal: When Khitan destroyed Jin, Zhang Yanzhe was first to enter the capital with troops; soldiers competed to enter Yu's house first, and his wealth was entirely gone in one night.

units.zh: 明日見彥澤，猶諂笑，自言願得持晉玉璽獻契丹，以冀恩獎。
units.en: The next day, when he met Yanzhe, he still fawned and smiled, saying he wished to carry Jin's imperial seal to present to the Khitan in hope of favor and reward.
units.literal: The next day when he saw Yanzhe he still fawned with smiles, saying of himself that he wished to be allowed to carry Jin's imperial seal to present to Khitan, hoping for favor and reward.

units.zh: 彥澤不納。
units.en: Yanzhe refused.
units.literal: Yanzhe would not accept it.

units.zh: 出帝之北，玉從入契丹，契丹以為太子太保。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor was taken north, Yu followed into Khitan territory, where the Khitan made him grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor went north, Yu followed and entered Khitan. Khitan made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 周廣順三年，其子傑自契丹逃歸，玉懼，以憂卒。
units.en: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, his son Jie escaped from Khitan and returned home. Yu, fearing reprisal, died of anxiety.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, his son Jie escaped from Khitan and returned. Yu was afraid and died from anxiety.

units.zh: 盧質字子徵，河南人也。
units.en: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, came from Henan.
units.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Zizheng, was a native of Henan.

units.zh: 父望，唐司勳郎中。
units.en: His father Wang had been a bureau director in the Tang Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: His father Wang served as a bureau director in the Tang Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 質幼聰惠，善屬文。
units.en: As a boy, Zhi was clever and skilled at writing.
units.literal: In youth Zhi was clever and skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 事唐為祕書郎，丁母憂，解職。
units.en: He served Tang as a secretary, then left office to mourn his mother.
units.literal: Serving Tang he was a secretary; when his mother died he left office in mourning.

units.zh: 後去遊太原，晉王以為河東節度掌書記。
units.en: Later he went to Taiyuan, where the Prince of Jin made him secretary of the Hedong military governorship.
units.literal: Later he traveled to Taiyuan and the Prince of Jin made him secretary of the Hedong military governorship.

units.zh: 質與張承業等定議立莊宗為嗣。
units.en: Zhi joined Zhang Chengye and others in resolving to install Zhuangzong as heir.
units.literal: Zhi, with Zhang Chengye and others, resolved to install Zhuangzong as heir.

units.zh: 莊宗將即位，以質為大禮使，拜行臺禮部尚書。
units.en: When Zhuangzong was about to take the throne, he made Zhi director of the great rites and appointed him minister of rites of the mobile administration.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to take the throne, he made Zhi director of the great rites and appointed him Minister of Rites of the mobile administration.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，欲以質為相。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne he wished to make Zhi chancellor.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he wished to make Zhi chancellor.

units.zh: 質性疎逸，不欲任責，因固辭不受。
units.en: Zhi was by nature casual and easygoing and did not wish to bear heavy responsibility, so he firmly declined.
units.literal: Zhi was by nature casual and retiring and did not wish to bear responsibility, so he firmly declined.

units.zh: 拜太原尹、北京留守，遷戶部尚書、翰林學士。
units.en: He was appointed metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan and protector of the Northern Capital, then promoted to minister of revenue and Hanlin academician.
units.literal: He was appointed metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan and protector of the Northern Capital, then transferred to Minister of Revenue and Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 從平梁，權判租庸，遷兵部尚書，後為學士承旨，仍賜「論思匡佐功臣」。
units.en: He followed the campaign to pacify Liang, acted as controller of the tax and corvée system, was promoted to minister of war, then became chief academician and was granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Counsel and Support."
units.literal: He followed the campaign to pacify Liang and acted as controller of the tax and corvée system, was transferred to Minister of War, then became chief academician and was granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Counsel and Support."

units.zh: 天成元年，拜匡國軍節度使。
units.en: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made military commissioner of the Kuangguo Army.
units.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of the Kuangguo Army.

units.zh: 三年，拜兵部尚書，判太常卿事。
units.en: In the third year he was made minister of war and overseer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: In the third year he was appointed Minister of War and overseer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 歷鎮河陽、橫海。
units.en: He served in succession as commissioner of Heyang and the Trans-Maritime circuit.
units.literal: He served in succession as commissioner of Heyang and the Trans-Maritime circuit.

units.zh: 初，梁已篡唐，封哀帝為濟陰王，既而酖殺之，瘞於曹州。
units.en: After the Later Liang usurped Tang, it enfeoffed Emperor Ai as Prince of Jiyin, then poisoned him and buried him at Cao Prefecture.
units.literal: At the beginning, after Liang had usurped Tang, it enfeoffed Emperor Ai as Prince of Jiyin; afterward it poisoned him and buried him at Cao Prefecture.

units.zh: 同光三年，莊宗將議改葬，而曹太后崩，乃止。
units.en: In the third year of Tongguang, Emperor Zhuangzong planned to discuss a proper reburial, but when Empress Dowager Cao died the matter was dropped.
units.literal: In the third year of Tongguang, Zhuangzong was about to discuss reburial, but Empress Dowager Cao died, and the matter was stopped.

units.zh: 因其故壟，稍廣其封，以時薦饗而已。
units.en: They merely enlarged the mound on its original site and offered seasonal sacrifices—nothing more.
units.literal: On his former mound they slightly enlarged the enclosure and offered seasonal sacrifices, and that was all.

units.zh: 質乃建議立廟追謚，謚曰昭宣光烈孝皇帝，廟號景宗。
units.en: Lu Zhi then proposed establishing a temple and conferring a posthumous title: Zhaoxuan Guanglie Xiao Emperor, with the temple name Jingzong.
units.literal: Zhi then proposed establishing a temple and conferring a posthumous title: posthumous name Zhaoxuan Guanglie Xiao, temple name Jingzong.

units.zh: 天成四年八月戍申，明宗禦文明殿，遣質奉冊立廟於曹州。
units.en: On day wushen of the eighth month in the fourth year of Tiancheng, Emperor Mingzong held court at the Hall of Civilizing Splendor and sent Lu Zhi to carry the patent and establish the temple at Cao Prefecture.
units.literal: In the eighth month, day wushen, of the fourth year of Tiancheng, Mingzong held court at the Hall of Civilizing Splendor and sent Zhi to carry the patent and establish the temple at Cao Prefecture.

units.zh: 而議者以謂輝王不幸為賊臣所立，而昭宗、何皇后皆為梁所弒，遂以亡國，而「昭宣光烈」非所宜稱，且立廟稱宗而不入太廟，皆非是。
units.en: Critics argued that Prince Hui had the misfortune of being installed by treacherous ministers, that Emperor Zhaozong and Empress He were both murdered by Liang, leading to the fall of the dynasty, that "Zhaoxuan Guanglie" was an inappropriate posthumous name, and that establishing a temple with the title "Zong" without admission to the Grand Ancestral Temple was all improper.
units.literal: But critics held that Prince Hui had the misfortune of being installed by treacherous ministers, and that Emperor Zhaozong and Empress He were both assassinated by Liang, leading to the fall of the state; that "Zhaoxuan Guanglie" was not a fitting designation, and moreover that establishing a temple and calling him "Zong" without entering the Grand Ancestral Temple—all were wrong.

units.zh: 共以此非質，大臣亦知其不可，乃奏去廟號。
units.en: All blamed Zhi for this. The senior ministers also knew it was wrong, and they memorialized to remove the temple name.
units.literal: All on this account criticized Zhi; the great ministers also knew it was impossible, and they submitted a memorial to remove the temple name.

units.zh: 秦王從榮坐謀反誅，質以右僕射權知河南府事。
units.en: When the Prince of Qin Congrong was executed for plotting rebellion, Lu Zhi, as right vice director of the Secretariat, was appointed acting prefect of Henan.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin Congrong was executed for plotting rebellion. Zhi, as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed acting prefect of Henan.

units.zh: 廢帝反鳳翔，湣帝發兵誅之，竭帑藏以厚賞，而兵至鳳翔皆叛降。
units.en: Emperor Fei rebelled at Fengxiang. Emperor Min sent troops against him and emptied the treasury for lavish rewards, but when the army reached Fengxiang the soldiers all defected and surrendered to Fei.
units.literal: Emperor Fei rebelled at Fengxiang. Emperor Min sent troops to execute him and emptied the treasury for generous rewards, but when the troops reached Fengxiang they all defected and surrendered.

units.zh: 廢帝悉將而東，事成許以重賞，而軍士皆過望。
units.en: Emperor Fei gathered all his generals and marched east, promising lavish rewards once victory was won, and the soldiers all expected far more than they would receive.
units.literal: Emperor Fei gathered all his generals and marched east, promising heavy rewards if they succeeded, and the soldiers all nurtured extravagant hopes.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，有司獻籍數甚少，廢帝暴怒。
units.en: When Emperor Fei took the throne, the responsible officials reported treasury figures that were shockingly low, and he flew into a rage.
units.literal: When Emperor Fei entered and took the throne, the responsible officials presented the registry figures, which were very small; Emperor Fei flew into a rage.

units.zh: 自諸鎮至刺史，皆進錢帛助國用，猶不足，三司使王玫請率民財以佐用。
units.en: From military commissioners down to prefects, all contributed money and silk to the treasury, yet it was still not enough. Wang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments, proposed levying the people's wealth to make up the shortfall.
units.literal: From military commissioners down to prefects, all contributed money and silk to aid state expenses, yet it was still insufficient. The commissioner of the Three Departments Wang Mei requested levying the people's wealth to supplement expenditures.

units.zh: 乃使質與玫等共議配率，而貧富不均，怨訟並起，囚系滿獄。
units.en: Lu Zhi and Wang Mei were then tasked with devising proportional levies, but the burden fell unevenly on rich and poor. Complaints and lawsuits multiplied, and the prisons filled.
units.literal: They then had Zhi and Mei and others jointly discuss proportional levies, but rich and poor were not equalized; complaints and lawsuits arose together, and the prisons filled with the imprisoned.

units.zh: 六七日間，所得不滿十萬。
units.en: In six or seven days the proceeds did not even reach one hundred thousand.
units.literal: In six or seven days the proceeds did not reach one hundred thousand.

units.zh: 廢帝患之，乃命質等借民屋課五月，由是民大咨怨。
units.en: Emperor Fei, vexed by this, ordered Lu Zhi and the others to levy five months' house rent on the people, provoking widespread outrage.
units.literal: Emperor Fei was troubled by this and ordered Zhi and the others to levy a five-month house tax on the people, whereupon the people greatly groaned with resentment.

units.zh: 晉高祖入立，質以疾分司西京，拜太子太保。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Lu Zhi, citing illness, served at the Western Capital branch office and was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin entered and took the throne, Zhi, on account of illness, served at the Western Capital branch office and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 卒，年七十六，贈太子太師，謚曰文忠。
units.en: He died at seventy-six. He was posthumously granted grand preceptor of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
units.literal: He died at age seventy-six. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

units.zh: 呂琦，字輝山，幽州安次人也。
units.en: Lü Qi, whose courtesy name was Huishan, came from Anci in You Prefecture.
units.literal: Lü Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was a native of Anci in You Prefecture.

units.zh: 父兗，為橫海軍節度判官。
units.en: His father Yan served as administrative aide to the military governor of the Henghai Army.
units.literal: His father Yan served as administrative aide to the military governor of the Henghai Army.

units.zh: 節度使劉守文與其弟守光以兵相攻，守文敗死，其吏民立其子延祚而事之，以兗為謀主。
units.en: The military governor Liu Shouwen and his younger brother Shouguang fought each other with troops. Shouwen was defeated and killed. His officials and people installed his son Yanzuo as ruler and made Yan their chief strategist.
units.literal: The military governor Liu Shouwen and his younger brother Shouguang attacked each other with troops. Shouwen was defeated and died. His officials and people installed his son Yanzuo and served him, making Yan the chief strategist.

units.zh: 已而延祚又為守光所敗，兗見殺。
units.en: Before long Yanzuo was defeated again by Shouguang, and Yan was put to death.
units.literal: Before long Yanzuo was again defeated by Shouguang, and Yan was killed.

units.zh: 守光怒兗，並族其家。
units.en: Shouguang, enraged at Yan, exterminated his entire clan.
units.literal: Shouguang, angry at Yan, exterminated his entire clan.

units.zh: 琦年十五，見執，將就刑，兗故客趙玉紿其監者曰：「此吾弟也。」
units.en: Qi was fifteen when he was seized and about to be executed. Zhao Yu, a former client of Yan, deceived the guard: "This is my younger brother."
units.literal: Qi was fifteen. Seized and about to be executed, Zhao Yu, a former client of Yan, deceived the guard saying: "This is my younger brother."

units.zh: 監者信之，縱琦去。
units.en: The guard believed him and let Qi go.
units.literal: The guard believed him and released Qi.

units.zh: 玉與琦得俱走，琦足弱不能行，玉負之而行，逾數百里，變姓名，乞食於道，以免。
units.en: Yu and Qi fled together. Qi's legs were too weak to walk, so Yu carried him on his back. They traveled several hundred li, changed their names, and begged for food along the road until they were safe.
units.literal: Yu and Qi were able to flee together. Qi's legs were weak and he could not walk; Yu carried him on his back. They traveled several hundred li, changed their names, and begged for food on the road, thus escaping.

units.zh: 琦為人美風儀，重節概，少喪其家，遊學汾、晉之間。
units.en: Lü Qi had a fine bearing and valued integrity. After losing his family while still young, he traveled to study in the Fen and Jin regions.
units.literal: Qi as a man had fine bearing and valued integrity. He lost his family while young and traveled to study between Fen and Jin.

units.zh: 唐莊宗鎮太原，以為代州軍事推官。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang held Taiyuan as his base, Qi was made military investigating officer of Dai Prefecture.
units.literal: When Tang's Zhuangzong held Taiyuan as his base, Qi was made military investigating officer of Dai Prefecture.

units.zh: 後為橫海趙德鈞節度推官，入為殿中侍御史。
units.en: He later served as investigating officer under Zhao Dejun, military governor of Henghai, and then entered the capital as palace attendant censor.
units.literal: Later he became investigating officer under Zhao Dejun, military governor of Henghai, and entered the capital as Palace Attendant Censor.

units.zh: 明宗時，為駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: Under Emperor Mingzong he served as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites for the Imperial Carriages, concurrently supervising censor overseeing miscellaneous matters.
units.literal: During Mingzong's time he was Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites for the Imperial Carriages, concurrently Supervising Censor overseeing miscellaneous matters.

units.zh: 河陽主藏吏盜所監物，下軍巡獄，獄吏尹訓納賂反其獄，其冤家訴於朝，下御史臺按驗，得訓贓狀，奏攝訓赴臺。
units.en: A treasurer clerk in Heyang stole goods under his charge and was sent to the military patrol prison. The prison clerk Yin Xun took a bribe and reversed the verdict. The aggrieved party appealed to the court, and the Censorate investigated, found evidence of Xun's corruption, and memorialized to summon him to the Censorate.
units.literal: A treasurer clerk of Heyang stole goods under his supervision and was sent down to the military patrol prison. The prison clerk Yin Xun accepted a bribe and reversed his case. His enemy appealed to the court; the case was sent down to the Censorate for investigation. They obtained evidence of Xun's corruption and memorialized to summon Xun to the Censorate.

units.zh: 訓為安重誨所庇，不與，琦請不已，訓懼自殺，獄乃辨，蒙活者甚眾。
units.en: Xun was protected by An Chonghui and was not surrendered. Qi pressed the matter relentlessly until Xun, in fear, killed himself. The cases were then cleared, and many who would have been condemned were spared.
units.literal: Xun was sheltered by An Chonghui and was not handed over. Qi pleaded without cease; Xun, in fear, killed himself. The cases were then cleared, and very many who would have been condemned were spared.

units.zh: 歲餘，遷禮部郎中、史館修撰。
units.en: After more than a year he was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

units.zh: 長興中，廢帝失守河中，罷居清化坊，與琦同巷，琦數往過之。
units.en: During the Changxing era, Emperor Fei lost Hezhong and was dismissed to live in Qinghua Ward. He lived on the same lane as Qi, and Qi often visited him.
units.literal: During Changxing, Emperor Fei lost control of Hezhong and was dismissed to live in Qinghua Ward. He was in the same lane as Qi, and Qi often went to visit him.

units.zh: 後廢帝入立，待琦甚厚，拜知制誥、給事中、樞密院直學士、端明殿學士。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Fei took the throne, he treated Qi with great favor, appointing him drafter of edicts, palace attendant, direct academician of the Privy Council, and academician of the Duanming Hall.
units.literal: Later when Emperor Fei entered and took the throne he treated Qi very generously, appointing him drafter of edicts, Palace Attendant, direct academician of the Privy Council, and academician of the Duanming Hall.

units.zh: 是時，晉高祖鎮河東，有二誌，廢帝患之，琦與李崧俱備顧問，多所裨畫。
units.en: At that time Gaozu of Jin held Hedong with divided loyalties, which troubled Emperor Fei. Qi and Li Song both served as his advisers and offered much useful counsel.
units.literal: At that time Gaozu of Jin was stationed at Hedong with double intent; Emperor Fei was troubled by it. Qi and Li Song were both retained as advisers and offered much useful counsel.

units.zh: 琦言：「太原之患，必引契丹為助，不如先事制之。」
units.en: Qi said: "The threat from Taiyuan will surely draw Khitan support. We would do better to forestall it."
units.literal: Qi said: "The trouble from Taiyuan will surely bring Khitan in as aid. It would be better to forestall it first."

units.zh: 自明宗時王都反定州，契丹遣禿餒、荝剌等助都，而為趙德鈞、王晏球所敗，禿餒見殺，荝剌等皆送京師。
units.en: Since Mingzong's time, when Wang Du rebelled at Ding Prefecture, the Khitan had sent Tu'nei, Cila, and others to aid him, but Zhao Dejun and Wang Yanqiu defeated them. Tu'nei was killed, and Cila and the others were sent to the capital.
units.literal: Since Mingzong's time, when Wang Du rebelled at Ding Prefecture, Khitan sent Tu'nei, Cila, and others to aid Du, but they were defeated by Zhao Dejun and Wang Yanqiu. Tu'nei was killed, and Cila and the rest were all sent to the capital.

units.zh: 其後契丹數遣使者求荝剌等，其辭甚卑恭，明宗輒斬其使者不報。
units.en: Afterward the Khitan repeatedly sent envoys requesting the return of Cila and the others, speaking with great humility, but Mingzong always executed their envoys and refused to reply.
units.literal: Afterward Khitan repeatedly sent envoys requesting Cila and the others. Their language was very humble and deferential, but Mingzong always executed their envoys and did not reply.

units.zh: 而東丹王又亡入中國，契丹由此數欲求和。
units.en: Moreover, the Prince of Dongdan had fled into China, and the Khitan had repeatedly sought peace as a result.
units.literal: Moreover the Prince of Dongdan again fled into China, and Khitan thereby repeatedly sought peace.

units.zh: 琦因言：「方今之勢，不如與契丹通和，如漢故事，歲給金帛，妻之以女，使強藩大鎮顧外無所引援，可弭其亂心。」
units.en: Qi went on: "Given the present situation, we would do better to make peace with the Khitan. Following Han precedent, we should send gold and silk each year and marry a princess to them, so that powerful frontier commanders would have no foreign ally to call upon. That could quell their rebellious ambitions."
units.literal: Qi thereupon said: "Given the present situation, we would do better to make peace with Khitan. Following Han precedent, we should give gold and silk each year and marry a princess to them, so that powerful frontier commanders, looking abroad, would have no external support to invoke. That could quell their rebellious intentions."

units.zh: 崧以琦語語三司使張延朗，延朗欣然曰：「茍能紓國患，歲費縣官十數萬緡，責吾取足可也！」
units.en: Li Song repeated Qi's words to Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the Three Departments. Yanlang said gladly: "If it can relieve the state's peril, spending several hundred thousand strings from the treasury each year—I can be tasked to supply whatever is needed!"
units.literal: Song repeated Qi's words to Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the Three Departments. Yanlang said gladly: "If it can relieve the state's peril, spending several hundred thousand strings from the treasury each year—I can be tasked to supply it fully!"

units.zh: 因共建其事。
units.en: They then jointly presented the proposal.
units.literal: They thereupon jointly presented the proposal.

units.zh: 廢帝大喜，佗日以琦等語問樞密直學士薛文遇，文遇大以為非，因誦戎昱「社稷依明主，安危托婦人」之詩，以誚琦等。
units.en: Emperor Fei was greatly pleased. Another day he asked Privy Direct Academician Xue Wenyü about Qi's proposal. Wenyü strongly objected and recited Rong Yu's verse, "The altars depend on a wise lord; safety and peril rest on a woman," to mock Qi and the others.
units.literal: Emperor Fei was greatly pleased. Another day he asked Privy Direct Academician Xue Wenyü about Qi's and the others' words. Wenyü strongly held it wrong and recited Rong Yu's verse "The altars depend on a wise lord; safety and peril rest on a woman," to mock Qi and the others.

units.zh: 廢帝大怒，急召崧、琦等問和戎計如何。
units.en: Emperor Fei was furious and urgently summoned Li Song, Lü Qi, and the others to explain their plan for peace with the Khitan.
units.literal: Emperor Fei was greatly enraged and urgently summoned Song, Qi, and the others to ask how their plan for peace with the barbarians was supposed to work.

units.zh: 琦等察帝色怒，亟曰：「臣等為國計，非與契丹求利於中國也。」
units.en: Qi and the others, seeing the emperor's anger, quickly said: "We propose this for the state's sake, not to seek profit from the Khitan at China's expense."
units.literal: Qi and the others, observing the emperor's angry countenance, quickly said: "Your servants propose this for the state's sake, not to seek profit from Khitan at China's expense."

units.zh: 帝即發怒曰：「卿等佐朕欲致太平而若是邪？
units.en: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "You who serve me in seeking peace would counsel me like this?
units.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry and said: "You who assist Us in seeking to bring about great peace—would act like this?

units.zh: 朕一女尚幼，欲棄之夷狄，金帛所以養士而捍國也，又輸以資虜，可乎？」
units.en: I have one daughter, still a child, and you would cast her off to the barbarians. Gold and silk are meant to support soldiers and defend the realm—can you truly mean to pour them out to feed our foes?"
units.literal: Our one daughter is still young, yet you would abandon her among the barbarians. Gold and silk exist to nourish soldiers and defend the state—is it permissible to hand them over to supply the enemy?"

units.zh: 崧等惶恐拜謝，拜無數，琦足力乏不能拜而先止。
units.en: Song and the others prostrated themselves in terror, bowing repeatedly without end. Qi's legs gave out from exhaustion and he stopped first, unable to keep bowing.
units.literal: Song and the others in fear and trepidation bowed in apology, bowing again and again without end. Qi's legs grew weak and he could not continue bowing, and stopped first.

units.zh: 帝曰：「呂琦強項，肯以人主視我邪！」
units.en: The emperor said, "Lü Qi is stiff-necked—does he not even regard me as his sovereign?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Lü Qi is stiff-necked—would he treat me as a lord of men?"

units.zh: 琦曰：「臣素病羸，拜多而乏，容臣少息。」
units.en: Qi said, "I have long been frail and sickly. These many bows have exhausted me—please allow me a moment to catch my breath."
units.literal: Qi said: "Your servant has long been sick and weak. From many bows I am exhausted—allow your servant a brief rest."

units.zh: 頃之喘定，奏曰：「陛下以臣等言非，罪之可也，雖拜何益？」
units.en: After a moment his breathing steadied. He said, "If Your Majesty finds us in the wrong, you may punish us. What good would more bowing do?"
units.literal: Shortly his breathing steadied, and he presented: "Your Majesty holds our words wrong—punishing us would be fitting. What use in bowing?"

units.zh: 帝意稍解，曰：「勿拜。」
units.en: The emperor's anger eased somewhat. "No more bowing," he said.
units.literal: The emperor's mind slightly eased, and he said: "Do not bow."

units.zh: 賜酒一卮而遣之，其議遂寢。
units.en: He gave them a cup of wine and sent them away, and the proposal was dropped.
units.literal: He bestowed one cup of wine and dismissed them; the proposal thereupon lapsed.

units.zh: 因遷琦御史中丞，居數月，復為端明殿學士。
units.en: Qi was made Vice Censor-in-Chief, and after several months was restored as Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity.
units.literal: Qi was therefore transferred to be Vice Censor-in-Chief; after several months he was again made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity.

units.zh: 其後晉高祖起太原，果引契丹為助，遂以亡唐。
units.en: Later, when Later Jin's Gaozu rose in Taiyuan, he did indeed enlist Khitan aid, and Tang was thereby overthrown.
units.literal: Afterward, Later Jin's Gaozu rose from Taiyuan, truly drawing the Khitan as aid, and thereby destroyed Tang.

units.zh: 琦事晉為秘書監，累遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: Qi served the Jin court as Director of the Secretariat and rose through several posts to Vice Minister of War.
units.literal: Qi served Jin as Director of the Secretariat and was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 天福八年卒。
units.en: He died in the eighth year of Tianfu.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died.

units.zh: 趙玉仕至職方員外郎，琦事之如父，玉疾，親嘗藥扶侍，及卒，為其家主辦喪葬。
units.en: Zhao Yu rose to the post of Assistant Director of the Bureau of Works. Qi treated him like a father—when Yu fell ill, Qi personally tasted his medicine and nursed him, and when he died, Qi arranged the funeral for his family.
units.literal: Zhao Yu rose in office to Assistant Director of the Bureau of Works. Qi served him as a father. When Yu fell ill, Qi personally tasted his medicine and attended him; when Yu died, Qi took charge of funeral arrangements for his household.

units.zh: 玉子文度幼孤，琦教以學，如己子，後舉進士及第云。
units.en: Yu's son Wendu was orphaned young. Qi educated him as if he were his own child, and Wendu later passed the jinshi examination, or so it is said.
units.literal: Yu's son Wendu was orphaned young; Qi taught him learning as his own son, and afterward he passed the jinshi examination, it is said.

units.zh: 琦有子餘慶、端。
units.en: Qi had two sons, Yuqing and Duan.
units.literal: Qi had sons Yuqing and Duan.

units.zh: 薛融，汾州平遙人也。
units.en: Xue Rong came from Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
units.literal: Xue Rong was a native of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

units.zh: 少以儒學知名，唐明宗時為右補闕，直弘文館。
units.en: He was known from youth for his classical learning. Under Tang Emperor Mingzong he served as Right Remonstrance Censor and was attached to the Hongwen Academy.
units.literal: In youth he was known for Confucian learning. In Tang Emperor Mingzong's time he served as Right Remonstrance Censor and attended the Hongwen Academy.

units.zh: 晉高祖鎮太原，融為觀察判官。
units.en: When Later Jin's Gaozu held Taiyuan, Rong served as his judicial adjutant on the observation staff.
units.literal: When Later Jin's Gaozu was military commissioner at Taiyuan, Rong was observation judicial adjutant.

units.zh: 高祖徙鄆，欲據太原拒命，延見賓佐，問以可否，而坐中或贊成之，或恐懼不敢言，融獨從容對曰：「融本儒生爾，軍旅之事，未嘗學也，進退存亡之理，豈易言哉！」
units.en: Gaozu moved to Yun, planning to hold Taiyuan and defy the throne. He summoned his staff to ask their view. Some in the room approved; others were too frightened to speak. Rong alone answered calmly: "I am only a Confucian scholar. I have never studied military affairs. How can one lightly pronounce on advance or retreat, on survival or ruin?"
units.literal: Gaozu moved to Yun, wished to hold Taiyuan and defy orders, and summoning guests and aides asked whether it was feasible. Among those seated some approved it, some in fear dared not speak. Rong alone calmly replied: "Rong is by origin a mere Confucian scholar. Matters of armies and campaigns I have never studied—the principle of advance or retreat, survival or extinction—how can it be lightly spoken?"

units.zh: 高祖不之責也。
units.en: Gaozu did not reproach him.
units.literal: Gaozu did not blame him.

units.zh: 高祖入立，拜吏部郎中，兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Rong was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and made Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous business.
units.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Rong was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Attending Censor overseeing miscellaneous affairs.

units.zh: 累拜左諫議大夫，遷中書舍人。
units.en: He rose through successive promotions to Left Grand Master for Remonstrance and then to Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
units.literal: In succession he was promoted to Left Grand Master for Remonstrance and transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 融曰：「文辭非臣所長也。」
units.en: Rong said, "Literary composition is not my strength."
units.literal: Rong said: "Literary composition is not what your servant excels at."

units.zh: 遂辭不拜。
units.en: He declined the post and did not accept it.
units.literal: He thereupon declined and did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 時詔修洛陽大內，融上疏切諫，高祖褒納其言，即詔罷其役。
units.en: When an edict ordered repairs on the Luoyang palace, Rong submitted a forceful memorial in protest. Gaozu praised his counsel, accepted it, and immediately halted the project.
units.literal: At the time an edict ordered repair of the Luoyang palace. Rong submitted a memorial vigorously remonstrating; Gaozu praised and accepted his words and immediately ordered the work stopped.

units.zh: 遷御史中丞，改尚書右丞，分司西京。
units.en: He was made Vice Censor-in-Chief, then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on detached duty at the Western Capital.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief, changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and served at the Western Capital on detached duty.

units.zh: 卒，年六十。
units.en: He died at the age of sixty.
units.literal: He died at age sixty.

units.zh: 何澤，廣州人也。
units.en: He Ze came from Guangzhou.
units.literal: He Ze was a native of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 父鼎，唐末為容管經略使。
units.en: His father Ding served in late Tang as military commissioner of Rong District.
units.literal: His father Ding in late Tang was military commissioner of Rong District.

units.zh: 澤少好學，長於歌詩。
units.en: Ze loved learning from youth and excelled in poetry.
units.literal: Ze in youth loved study and excelled at songs and verse.

units.zh: 舉進士，為洛陽令。
units.en: After passing the jinshi examination, he became magistrate of Luoyang.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Luoyang.

units.zh: 唐莊宗好畋獵，數踐民田，澤乃潛身伏草間伺莊宗，當馬諫曰：「陛下未能一天下以休兵，而暴斂疲民以給軍食。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang loved the hunt and often rode through the people's fields. Ze hid in the grass along the route and stepped before the emperor's horse to remonstrate: "Your Majesty has not yet unified the realm and brought the armies to rest, yet you levy harshly on an exhausted people to feed the troops.
units.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong loved hunting and repeatedly trampled the people's fields. Ze then hid himself in the grass to watch for Zhuangzong, blocking his horse and remonstrating: "Your Majesty has not yet unified the realm to rest the armies, yet you violently extract from the exhausted people to supply military provisions.

units.zh: 今田將熟，奈何恣畋遊以害多稼？
units.en: The crops are nearly ripe—how can you ride about freely and ruin the harvest?
units.literal: Now the fields are about to ripen—how can you indulgently hunt and harm the abundant grain?

units.zh: 使民何以出租賊，吏以何督民耕？
units.en: How then are the people to pay their taxes, and how are officials to supervise the planting?
units.literal: How can the people pay taxes and rents, and how can officials compel the people to farm?

units.zh: 陛下不聽臣言，願賜臣死於馬前，使後世知陛下之過。」
units.en: If Your Majesty will not listen, grant me death here before your horse, so that posterity may know where the blame lies."
units.literal: If Your Majesty will not heed your servant's words, I wish to be granted death before your horse, so that later ages may know Your Majesty's fault."

units.zh: 莊宗大笑，為之止獵。
units.en: Zhuangzong laughed heartily and stopped the hunt.
units.literal: Zhuangzong laughed greatly and for his sake stopped the hunt.

units.zh: 拜倉部郎中。
units.en: He was appointed Director in the Granary Office.
units.literal: He was appointed Director in the Granary Office.

units.zh: 明宗時，數上書言事。
units.en: Under Emperor Mingzong he repeatedly submitted memorials on state affairs.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴州，又欲幸鄴，而人情不便，大臣屢言不聽；
units.en: Emperor Mingzong visited Bianzhou and then wished to visit Ye as well, but the people found the prospect unwelcome. The senior ministers remonstrated repeatedly, but the emperor would not listen.
units.literal: Mingzong visited Bian Prefecture, then wished also to visit Ye, but the people's sentiment found it inconvenient; grand ministers repeatedly spoke but he would not listen.

units.zh: 澤伏閤切諫，明宗嘉之，拜吏部郎中、史館修撰。
units.en: Ze knelt at the gate in urgent remonstrance. Mingzong praised him and made him Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Compiler in the Historiographical Institute.
units.literal: Ze prostrated himself at the gate and urgently remonstrated. Mingzong commended him and appointed him Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Compiler of the Historiographical Institute.

units.zh: 澤外雖直言，而內實邪佞，嘗於內殿起居，班退，獨留，以笏叩顙，北望而呼曰：「明主，明主！」
units.en: Though Ze spoke bluntly in public, in private he was sly and fawning. Once at court in the inner hall, when the officials withdrew he alone remained, bowing and striking his forehead with his tablet as he faced north, crying, "Wise sovereign! Wise sovereign!"
units.literal: Ze outwardly remonstrated directly, yet inwardly was truly sly and fawning. Once at morning attendance in the inner hall, when the court withdrew he alone remained, striking his forehead with his tablet, facing north and calling: "Bright lord! Bright lord!"

units.zh: 聞者皆哂之。
units.en: All who heard laughed at him.
units.literal: Those who heard all sneered at him.

units.zh: 五代之際，民苦於兵，往往因親疾以割股，或既喪而割乳廬墓，以規免州縣賦役。
units.en: In the age of the Five Dynasties the people were worn down by war. Many, when a parent fell ill, cut flesh from their own thighs as an offering, or after a parent's death mutilated themselves and lived in mourning huts by the grave, all to win exemption from local taxes and corvée.
units.literal: In the age of the Five Dynasties the people suffered from warfare and often, because of a parent's illness, cut flesh from their thighs, or after bereavement cut their breasts and built hut-tombs, seeking to evade prefectural and county taxes and corvée.

units.zh: 戶部歲給蠲符，不可勝數，而課州縣出紙，號為「蠲紙」。
units.en: The Ministry of Revenue issued so many tax-exemption certificates each year that the number was beyond counting, yet it assessed the prefectures and counties for the paper to print them—paper called "exemption paper."
units.literal: The Ministry of Revenue annually issued exemption certificates beyond counting, yet assessed prefectures and counties for paper, called "exemption paper."

units.zh: 澤上書言其敝，明宗下詔悉廢戶部蠲紙。
units.en: Ze submitted a memorial describing this abuse, and Mingzong issued an edict abolishing the Ministry's exemption paper entirely.
units.literal: Ze submitted a memorial stating its abuses; Mingzong issued an edict abolishing entirely the Ministry's exemption paper.

units.zh: 澤與宰相趙鳳有舊，數私於鳳，求為給諫。
units.en: Ze had old ties with Chief Minister Zhao Feng and repeatedly visited him in private, seeking a post as remonstrance censor.
units.literal: Ze had old ties with chief minister Zhao Feng and repeatedly sought him out privately, asking to be made remonstrance censor.

units.zh: 鳳薄其為人，以為太常少卿。
units.en: Feng disdained his character and had him appointed Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship instead.
units.literal: Feng looked down on his character and had him made Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.

units.zh: 敕未出而澤先知之，即稱新官上章自訴。
units.en: Before the edict was even issued, Ze already knew of it. He immediately assumed the new title and submitted a memorial in his own defense.
units.literal: Before the edict was issued Ze already knew beforehand, and immediately styled himself by the new title and submitted a memorial in self-defense.

units.zh: 章下中書，鳳等言：「澤未拜命而稱新官，輕侮朝廷，請坐以法。」
units.en: When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Feng and the others said, "Ze has styled himself by a new office before receiving appointment. This shows contempt for the court. We ask that he be punished according to law."
units.literal: The memorial reached the Secretariat; Feng and the others said: "Ze has not received appointment yet styles himself by a new office—he lightly insults the court. We ask that he be punished according to law."

units.zh: 乃以太僕少卿致仕，居於河陽。
units.en: He was retired as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and went to live at Heyang.
units.literal: He was therefore retired as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and dwelt at Heyang.

units.zh: 澤時年已七十，尚希仕進，即遣婢宜子詣匭上章言事，請立秦王為皇太子。
units.en: By then Ze was already seventy, yet still hungered for office. He sent his maid Yizi to deposit a memorial asking that the Prince of Qin be made crown prince.
units.literal: Ze was then already seventy years old, yet still hoped for advancement in office, and dispatched his maid Yizi to the memorial box to submit a memorial on affairs, asking that the Prince of Qin be established as crown prince.

units.zh: 秦王素驕，多不軌，遂成其禍，由澤而始。
units.en: The Prince of Qin was arrogant and repeatedly overstepped propriety. The disaster that followed began with Ze.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin was by nature arrogant and often overstepped bounds; the calamity was thereby brought about, beginning with Ze.

units.zh: 晉高祖入立，召為太常少卿，以疾卒於家。
units.en: When Later Jin's Gaozu took the throne, Ze was recalled as Vice Director of Sacrificial Worship, but died of illness at home.
units.literal: When Later Jin's Gaozu entered and took the throne, Ze was summoned as Vice Director of Sacrificial Worship and died of illness at home.

units.zh: 王權，字秀山，太原人也。
units.en: Wang Quan, whose courtesy name was Xiushan, came from Taiyuan.
units.literal: Wang Quan, courtesy name Xiushan, was a native of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 唐左僕射起之曾孫。
units.en: He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Director Wang Qi.
units.literal: He was the great-grandson of Tang Left Vice Director Wang Qi.

units.zh: 父蕘，官至右司郎中。
units.en: His father Rao rose to the post of Director of the Right Office.
units.literal: His father Rao rose to office as Director of the Right Office.

units.zh: 權舉進士，為右補闕。
units.en: Quan passed the jinshi examination and served as Right Remonstrance Censor.
units.literal: Quan passed the jinshi and served as Right Remonstrance Censor.

units.zh: 唐亡，事梁為職方員外郎、知制誥、翰林學士，累遷御史中丞。
units.en: After Tang fell he served the Liang as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Appointments, Drafting Secretary, and Hanlin Academician, and rose in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: When Tang fell he served Liang as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Appointments, Drafting Edicts, and Hanlin Academician, rising in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，貶權隨州司馬。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Quan was demoted to army aide at Suizhou.
units.literal: When Tang's Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Quan was demoted to Suizhou Army Aide.

units.zh: 起為右庶子，累遷戶部尚書。
units.en: He was recalled as Right Subordinate Director and rose in succession to Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: He was raised to Right Subordinate Director and promoted in succession to Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 晉高祖時為兵部尚書。
units.en: Under Later Jin's Gaozu he served as Minister of War.
units.literal: In Later Jin Gaozu's time he was Minister of War.

units.zh: 是時，高祖以父事契丹，權當奉使，嘆曰：「我雖不才，安能稽顙於穹廬乎？」
units.en: At that time Gaozu treated the Khitan like a father-lord. Quan was to serve as envoy and sighed, "Though I am no great man, how could I kowtow in a nomad tent?"
units.literal: At this time Gaozu treated the Khitan as a father; Quan was to serve as envoy and sighed: "Though I am without talent, how can I kowtow in a nomad tent?"

units.zh: 因辭不行，坐是停任。
units.en: He declined and refused to go, and for this was suspended from office.
units.literal: He therefore declined and would not go, and for this reason was suspended from office.

units.zh: 踰年以太子少傅致仕。
units.en: More than a year later he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: After more than a year he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 卒，年七十八，贈左僕射。
units.en: He died at the age of seventy-eight and was posthumously granted the title of Left Vice Director.
units.literal: He died at age seventy-eight and was posthumously granted Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 史圭，常山石邑人也。
units.en: Shi Gui came from Shiyi in Changshan.
units.literal: Shi Gui was a native of Shiyi in Changshan.

units.zh: 為人明敏好學。
units.en: He was bright, quick-witted, and fond of learning.
units.literal: As a man he was bright, quick, and fond of learning.

units.zh: 為寧晉、樂壽縣令，有善政，縣人立碑以頌之。
units.en: As magistrate of Ningjin and Leshou he governed well, and the people of both counties erected stelae in his praise.
units.literal: He served as magistrate of Ningjin and Leshou, had good governance, and the county people erected stelae to praise him.

units.zh: 郭崇韜鎮成德，辟為從事。
units.en: When Guo Chongtao was military commissioner of Chengde, he recruited Gui as an aide.
units.literal: When Guo Chongtao was military commissioner of Chengde, he recruited Gui as an aide.

units.zh: 明宗時，為尚書郎。
units.en: Under Emperor Mingzong he served as a Director in the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time he was a Director in the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 安重誨為樞密使，薦圭直學士。
units.en: When An Chonghui was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he recommended Gui as Direct Academician.
units.literal: An Chonghui was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and recommended Gui as Direct Academician.

units.zh: 故事，直學士職雖清，而承領文書，參掌庶務，與判官無異。
units.en: By precedent, though the Direct Academician's post was prestigious, he handled documents and shared in routine business no differently from a judicial adjutant.
units.literal: By precedent, though the Direct Academician's post was exalted, he received documents and took part in miscellaneous affairs, no different from a judicial adjutant.

units.zh: 重誨素不知書，倚圭以備顧問，始白許圭升殿侍立。
units.en: An Chonghui was no scholar himself and relied on Gui for counsel. He was the first to request that Gui be allowed to ascend the hall and attend the emperor standing.
units.literal: An Chonghui by nature did not know books and relied on Gui for consultation; he first requested permission for Gui to ascend the hall and attend standing.

units.zh: 樞密直學士升殿自圭始。
units.en: The practice of Direct Academicians of the Bureau ascending the imperial hall began with Gui.
units.literal: Direct Academicians of the Bureau ascending the hall began with Gui.

units.zh: 改尚書右丞，判吏部銓事。
units.en: He was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and placed in charge of Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.
units.literal: He was changed to Right Vice Director and judged Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.

units.zh: 重誨敗死，圭出為貝州刺史。
units.en: When An Chonghui fell and was executed, Gui was sent out as prefect of Beizhou.
units.literal: When An Chonghui was defeated and died, Gui went out as prefect of Beizhou.

units.zh: 罷歸常山，閉門絕人事，出入閭里乘輜軿車。
units.en: After his dismissal he returned to Changshan, shut his door to the world, and when he went about the neighborhood he rode in a small covered carriage.
units.literal: Dismissed he returned to Changshan, shut his door and cut off human affairs; going in and out of the lanes he rode a small covered carriage.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，召拜刑部侍郎、鹽鐵副使，遷吏部侍郎，分知銓事，有能名。
units.en: When Later Jin's Gaozu took the throne, Gui was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Salt and Iron Commissioner, then promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel with shared charge of selection affairs, and earned a reputation for competence.
units.literal: When Later Jin's Gaozu took the throne, Gui was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Salt and Iron Commissioner, transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, shared in selection affairs, and had a reputation for ability.

units.zh: 以疾罷，卒於常山。
units.en: He was dismissed because of illness and died at Changshan.
units.literal: He was dismissed due to illness and died at Changshan.

units.zh: 龍敏，字欲訥，幽州永清人也。
units.en: Long Min, whose courtesy name was Yunè, came from Yongqing in You Prefecture.
units.literal: Long Min, courtesy name Yunè, was a native of Yongqing in You Prefecture.

units.zh: 少仕州，攝參軍。
units.en: In youth he served the prefecture as acting adjutant.
units.literal: In youth he served the prefecture, acting as adjutant.

units.zh: 劉守光亂，敏避之滄州，遂客於梁，久不調。
units.en: When Liu Shouguang rebelled, Min fled to Cangzhou and then lived as a guest in Liang, long without receiving an appointment.
units.literal: When Liu Shouguang rebelled, Min fled to Cangzhou, then sojourned in Liang, long without promotion.

units.zh: 敏素善馮道，道為唐莊宗從事，乃潛往依之。
units.en: Min had long been on good terms with Feng Dao. When Dao became an aide to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, Min secretly went to join him.
units.literal: Min had long been friendly with Feng Dao; Dao was Zhuangzong's aide, and Min secretly went to rely on him.

units.zh: 監軍張承業謂道曰：「聞子有客，可與俱來。」
units.en: Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye said to Dao, "I hear you have a guest. Bring him with you."
units.literal: Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye said to Dao: "I hear you have a guest—he may come with you."

units.zh: 道以敏見承業，承業辟敏監軍巡官，使掌奏記。
units.en: Dao introduced Min to Chengye, who recruited Min as touring officer on the army supervisor's staff and put him in charge of memorials and correspondence.
units.literal: Dao presented Min to Chengye; Chengye recruited Min as army supervisor touring officer and had him manage memorials and letters.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，召拜司門員外郎。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Min was summoned and appointed Assistant Director of the Gate Office.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Min was summoned as Assistant Director of the Gate Office.

units.zh: 敏父咸式，年七十餘，而其祖父年九十餘，皆在鄴，敏乃求為興唐尹，事祖、父以孝聞。
units.en: Min's father Xianshi was over seventy, and his grandfather over ninety; both lived at Ye. Min therefore asked to be appointed Xingtang Prefect so he could serve them, and became known for his filial devotion.
units.literal: Min's father Xianshi was over seventy, and his grandfather over ninety; both were at Ye. Min therefore asked to be Xingtang Prefect and served grandfather and father, famed for filial piety.

units.zh: 丁母憂，去職。
units.en: When his mother died he left office to observe mourning.
units.literal: He mourned his mother and left office.

units.zh: 趙在禮反，逼敏起視事。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, he forced Min to leave mourning and resume office.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, he forced Min to rise and attend to affairs.

units.zh: 明宗即位，在禮鎮滄州，敏乃復得居喪。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Zaili was posted to Cangzhou as military commissioner, and Min was able to return to mourning.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zaili was military commissioner at Cangzhou, and Min was again able to observe mourning.

units.zh: 服除，累拜兵部侍郎。
units.en: After mourning ended he rose in succession to Vice Minister of War.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 馮赟留守北京，辟敏副留守。
units.en: When Feng Yun was left behind to guard Beijing, he recruited Min as his deputy.
units.literal: Feng Yun was left behind to guard Beijing and recruited Min as deputy left-behind commissioner.

units.zh: 赟入為樞密使，敏拜吏部侍郎。
units.en: When Yun entered the capital as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Min was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: Yun entered as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Min was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 是時，晉高祖起太原，乞兵契丹。
units.en: At that time Later Jin's Gaozu rose in Taiyuan and sought Khitan troops.
units.literal: At this time Later Jin's Gaozu rose in Taiyuan and begged troops from the Khitan.

units.zh: 唐廢帝在懷州，趙德鈞父子有異志，張敬達屯於晉安，勢甚危急。
units.en: Emperor Fei of Tang was at Huai Prefecture. Zhao Dejun and his son harbored disloyal ambitions, while Zhang Jingda was encamped at Jin'an. The situation was extremely perilous.
units.literal: Tang Emperor Fei was at Huai Prefecture; Zhao Dejun and his son harbored disloyal designs; Zhang Jingda was encamped at Jin'an—the situation was extremely perilous.

units.zh: 廢帝問計從臣，敏曰：「晉所恃者契丹也。
units.en: Emperor Fei asked his ministers for counsel. Min said, "Jin relies on the Khitan.
units.literal: Emperor Fei asked his following ministers for plans. Min said: "What Jin relies on is the Khitan.

units.zh: 東丹王失國之君，今在京師，若以兵送東丹自幽州而入西樓，契丹且有內顧之憂，何暇助晉？
units.en: The Prince of Dongdan is a deposed ruler now held in the capital. If we send troops to escort him from You Prefecture into Xilou, the Khitan will have troubles at home. What time will they have to aid Jin?
units.literal: The Prince of Dongdan is a deposed lord; he is now in the capital. If troops escort Dongdan from You Prefecture to enter Xilou, the Khitan will have inward anxiety—what leisure to aid Jin?

units.zh: 晉失契丹，大事去矣。」
units.en: Once Jin loses Khitan support, the cause is lost."
units.literal: Once Jin loses the Khitan, the great affair is lost."

units.zh: 又謂李懿曰：「敏，燕人也，能知德鈞。
units.en: He also said to Li Yi, "I am a man of Yan and know Dejun well.
units.literal: He also said to Li Yi: "Min is a man of Yan and can know Dejun.

units.zh: 德鈞為將，守城嬰塹，篤勵健兒而已。
units.en: As a general Dejun is good only at holding cities and keeping to the trenches, heartening his stout fighters—that is all.
units.literal: As a general Dejun merely holds cities and keeps to trenches, earnestly encouraging brave warriors—that is all.

units.zh: 使其當大敵，奮不顧身，非其能也。
units.en: Set him against a great enemy and expect him to throw away his life without hesitation—that is not in his nature.
units.literal: To set him against a great enemy, risking his life without regard for himself—that is not within his capacity.

units.zh: 況有異志乎？
units.en: And does he not already harbor disloyal ambitions?
units.literal: Moreover, does he not harbor disloyal designs?

units.zh: 今聞駕前之馬，猶有五千，願得壯者千匹，健兵千人，與勇將郎萬金，自平遙沿山冒虜中而趨官砦，且戰且行，得其半達，則事濟矣！」
units.en: I hear there are still five thousand horses with the imperial train. Give me a thousand strong mounts, a thousand fit soldiers, and the brave general Lang Wanjin, and I will strike from Pingyao along the mountains through enemy territory toward the government camp, fighting as we march. If even half of us arrive, the task can still be accomplished!"
units.literal: Now I hear the horses before the imperial carriage still number five thousand. I wish to obtain a thousand strong mounts, a thousand fit soldiers, and the brave general Lang Wanjin, to proceed from Pingyao along the mountains through the enemy's midst toward the official fort, fighting as we march—if half can arrive, the affair will succeed!"

units.zh: 懿為言之廢帝，廢帝莫能用。
units.en: Li Yi relayed this to Emperor Fei, but the emperor could not adopt the plan.
units.literal: Yi relayed this to Emperor Fei; Emperor Fei could not employ it.

units.zh: 然人皆壯其大言。
units.en: Yet everyone admired the boldness of his words.
units.literal: Yet all admired his bold words.

units.zh: 歷晉為太常卿，使於吳越。
units.en: Through the Jin dynasty he served as Director of Sacrificial Worship and was sent as envoy to Wuyue.
units.literal: Through Jin he served as Director of Sacrificial Worship and was envoy to Wuyue.

units.zh: 是時，使吳越者，見吳越王皆下拜，敏獨揖之。
units.en: At that time envoys to Wuyue all prostrated themselves before the King of Wuyue; Min alone gave a formal bow with clasped hands.
units.literal: At that time envoys to Wuyue all bowed low before the King of Wuyue; Min alone made a clasped-hand salute.

units.zh: 還，遷工部侍郎。
units.en: On his return he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
units.literal: On return he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 乾祐元年，瘍發於首卒，贈右僕射。
units.en: In the first year of Qianyou a carbuncle broke out on his head and he died. He was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianyou an ulcer broke out on his head and he died; he was posthumously granted Right Vice Censor.
